svg.text: KV CACHE & PREFIX CACHING: END-TO-END SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
From Stateless Workloads to Attention Mechanics, Sizing, Storage Tiering & Offload Execution
1. THE WORKLOAD PROBLEM: STATELESS API CALLS & REPEATED PREFIXES (40%–90% REDUNDANT TOKENS)
1 copy held in cache across N requests
2. TRANSFORMER INFERENCE PHASES: PREFILL vs. DECODE
Generates KV Cache for prompt + Outputs 1st Token ("keys")
Metric: TTFT (Time To First Token) — Quadratic O(N²) Attention
Reads all prior K & V vectors per step without recomputing
Appends new token's K & V to existing cache pool
3. INSIDE A TRANSFORMER LAYER: WHY WE CACHE "K" & "V" (AND DROP "Q")
1. New Q scored against all past K
Past K & V never change once computed
and are read by EVERY future token.
Result: Stored in KV Cache Pool
4. KV CACHE SIZING MATHEMATICS (EXAMPLE: QWEN3-32B CONFIG.JSON)
Bytes / Token = 2 (K & V) × Layers (64) × KV Heads (8 via GQA) × Head Dim (128) × Precision (2 Bytes @ BF16) = 256 KB / Token
Strict Rule: Exact token match from index 0
5. MEMORY & STORAGE HIERARCHY: WHERE TO KEEP EVICTED KV CACHES
THE STORAGE vs. RECOMPUTE CROSSOVER RULE
Prefill compute scales quadratically O(N²) with prompt length, while fetching bytes scales linearly O(N). Offloading wins whenever T_fetch < T_recompute.
6. LAB PROOF FLOW: vLLM + LMCACHE + NVMe (QWEN3-32B, 8,192 TOKENS, 16 GB KV POOL)
PATH A: COLD RUN (Cache Miss → Compute & Offload)
NVMe Hit Tokens: 0 (No prior prefix match on disk)
Populates active 16 GB GPU KV Pool
Writes 8 files per slice → 32 files × 64 MB = 2.0 GB total
(Request waits only for GPU memory copy, not disk I/O)
OS page cache flushed to force true hardware NVMe read next
PATH B: WARM RUN (Cache Hit → Fetch from NVMe)
2. Direct NVMe Read into GPU KV Pool
Streams 32 chunk files (~2 GB) from NVMe SSD into GPU Pool
Loads K & V for first 8,191 tokens without GPU math
3. Minimal Compute on Final Token Only
Engine computes only the final (8,192nd) token against
the restored KV cache to generate the 1st output token
4. First Token Emitted Much Sooner (Fast TTFT)
Skips full prefill compute & frees GPU cycles for other users
